source.statement: under of the edge push_up ⇒ causally_open (witness Causal.Causality.causallyOpen_of_pushUp): 'for every open V and v ∈ V there are p, p' ∈ V with p ≪_V v and v ≪_V p''

hypotheses.paper: hZm: ∀ V, ∀ v ∈ V, ∃ p ∈ V, p ≪_V v; hZp: the same to the future

findings: causallyOpen_of_pushUp (Causal/LemmaK.lean:93) and causallyOpenFuture_of_pushUp (:82) are model-free but sit in a model-importing module; they are re-proved here (same four-line proof) as PushUp.causallyOpenFuture_of_chronalPastNeighbours / PushUp.causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours: a duplicate for T-abs-hoist-model-free (kb/0047's list should gain them).

Chronal neighbours are not implied by push-up, causal openness, global hyperbolicity and no causal endpoint together: the lightlike line has all four and an empty chronology (Causal.lightlikeLine_separates_chronalNeighbours). So the converse of push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open fails, and the side condition of that edge is genuine.

Under absolute minimality on a T1 space, ChronalPastNeighbours is exactly 'I⁻(x) ≠ ∅ for every x' (AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff); with ChronalNeighbours every point is strongly tarentin (in Z⁺ and Z⁻) with no hypothesis.
questions: Base direction of the one-sided notion: the library's convention puts the future as base (CausallyOpenFuture). I took the past as base (ChronalPastNeighbours; the future form is C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours), because the witnesses take hZm first and past neighbours are what give FUTURE causal openness, so the future theorem stays the base one (kb/0002). Renaming before graduation is cheap if the author or keeper prefers ChronalFutureNeighbours.

Not to be merged with HasChronalNeighbour of the in-flight CausalScaffold.LocateExtension (one point, either side, chronology in M): ChronalNeighbours is both sides, at every point of every open V, chronology in V.

It is not tarentin, so this does not separate no_causal_endpoint from GH ∧ tarentin ∧ causally arc-connected, the hypotheses of the nesting theorem.

The witnesses with hJm/hJp in model-importing modules (Lemma K in Causal.LemmaK; Inextensible.not_forall_le_of_causallyCompact, not_forall_ge_…, causallyCompleteCurves_of_causallyCompact in Causal.ChainsCurves) cannot be restated in layer 1; they take NoCausalEndpoint's two components verbatim, so restating them after a hoist is one line each.
questions: Base direction: past (NoPastEndpoint; the future form is C.dual.NoPastEndpoint), for the same reason as ChronalPastNeighbours (the witnesses take hpast/hJm first; Geroch's lt_ne uses J⁻ alone). Whether the keeper wants a one-sided node no_past_endpoint as well is open; only the two-sided one was asked.

findings: ERS write ∂U₁ \ ∂S (eperon2018predictability.txt:2029). Both readings of ∂S, the frontier of the hypersurface S in R^{d+1} (= closure S) and its edge (closure S \ S), give the same set of boundary points, since S ⊆ U₁ misses frontier U₁ (U₁ open); the Lean form frontier U₁ \ closure S is therefore not a choice.
questions: OneSidedBoundary is not a property of a causality: it is a predicate on an open set U and an excluded set B (pure topology). It fits neither sort of programme/ladder.toml (causality: a predicate on one C; geometry: on a CBG geometry). Reading taken: defined in namespace Causal.Causality as the dispatch asks, with no C argument; the keeper must decide whether one_sided_boundary becomes a node of a new sort or stays an `under` in words naming Causal.Causality.OneSidedBoundary.

Reading taken for the node one_sided_boundary of T-lad-development-nodes: the topological content (OneSidedAt at each boundary point off closure S), not the chart condition (4.83) itself, which needs a manifold structure and is layer 3.
